# Analyschefen: ”Kommer berätta för mina barnbarn om 2026”

**Feed**: borslunch  
**Published**: 2026-09-17  
**Market Sentiment**: Mixed

⏱️ **Time Horizon Key**: ST = <3 months | MT = 3-12 months | LT = >12 months

---

## Episode Thesis

Börslunch (EFN) on 17 Sep 2026 looks at the macro picture after the Fed rate hike. Rising rates, not AI, are now seen as the market's biggest fear. Guest Gabriella Sahlman of Fuels Capital covers private credit: its rapid growth, weak loan structures, liquidity-mismatched funds and the risk from debt-financed AI capex. Pareto's head of research Eirik Havaldsen is very bullish on shipping. He calls the tanker market (Frontline) historic and sees a structural supercycle in car carriers (Wallenius Wilhelmsen) driven by Chinese car exports.

---

## Universe Stocks

### 🟢 FRO — Frontline | **BUY** (Strong)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: ST  
**Confidence**: 75%

Pareto's Havaldsen: tanker market historically extreme in 2026, entering peak season at record levels, could go further.

#### Reasoning

Cited analyst (Pareto head of research, not host) argues Hormuz/Middle East conflict made a third of crude trade far less efficient, boosting tanker earnings to extreme levels (vessel cost recouped ~25%/month in cash flow). Peak winter season ahead from already-historic highs. He acknowledges it is cyclical and will not last indefinitely, so horizon is short.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Middle East/Hormuz disruptions resolve and trade efficiency normalises
- if peak-season rates fail to materialise
- cyclical downturn in tanker rates

> *"Den marknaden är så bra att jag kommer att berätta för mina barnbarn om 2026."*

---

### 🟢 WAWI — Wallenius Wilhelmsen | **BUY** (Moderate)

**Sentiment**: Positive | **Time Horizon**: LT  
**Confidence**: 65%

Pareto's Havaldsen positive on car carriers: structural supercycle driven by China becoming world's largest car exporter.

#### Reasoning

Cited analyst view: China exports went from ~1m to ~11m cars, creating trade imbalance and ballast legs that owners get paid for, leading to a supercycle. The rest of the world is buying cheap Chinese cars. Risk: Europe could follow the US in tariffing Chinese cars.

#### Sell Triggers

- if Europe imposes heavy tariffs on Chinese cars
- if Chinese car export growth stalls
- fleet overcapacity from newbuilds

> *"Så det är en trend som bara växer och då har du Wallenius Wilderlund som tjänar på det."*
